date_note: The Epoch Times (21 Nov) says Trump selected Davies on Thursday, 19 November; the White House release was not read.
exec: Leadership change at the US office that coordinates national cyber policy; may affect federal cyber priorities and planned programs.
org: Office of the National Cyber Director
plain: Sean Cairncross is out as US national cyber director. Nextgov/FCW says Jay Clayton will lead the office temporarily while Kirsten Davies, the Pentagon's chief information officer, awaits Senate confirmation.
summary: SecurityWeek reports Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies was appointed National Cyber Director, replacing Sean Cairncross. Nextgov/FCW reports on 23 November that a White House official confirmed Director of National Intelligence Jay Clayton will temporarily lead the office while Davies seeks Senate confirmation. The Epoch Times quotes Trump on Cairncross's firing: "Because I didn't think that person was good enough."
title: Pentagon CIO Kirsten Davies named US national cyber director as Sean Cairncross leaves

validation.note: SecurityWeek and The Epoch Times (both 21 Nov, read 22 Nov) each state the appointment; The Epoch Times quotes Trump on the firing; the whitehouse.gov release SecurityWeek links was not read. Earlier: Nextgov/FCW (cites Axios) and CyberScoop (anonymous source close to the White House, no Axios citation) read. Anadolu (Nov 20) says a White House official confirmed the departure and that Secretary of State Rubio congratulated Davies as new director on X; Gizmodo calls her acting director and says the reason was not officially stated. Reasons for departure differ in coverage and are not stated here as fact. Update 23 Nov: Nextgov/FCW (read) says a White House official confirmed Clayton's interim role and Davies's Senate confirmation process.
